messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — our weekly RFC/design sync is becoming painful for APAC and some PST folks. The current Tuesday 9am PT slot hits late evening for Tokyo and is during on-call for a couple people. Can we pick a rotation or staggered schedule? :calendar:
maya: Yeah, noticed that too. We had 3 people drop off last week. :frowning: I can do a rotation: EU-friendly one week, APAC-friendly next, then PST-friendly.
samir: Rotation sounds reasonable. Curious if we can automate invites so the recurrence uses multiple rules instead of a single recurring event that always shows the wrong local time.
jen: If we rotate, can we keep the first-Tuesday-of-month slot reserved for quick canary/risk reviews? Those need most of the senior folks.
alex: Good call. Proposal:
- Week A: 08:00 UTC (works for EU, OK for PST early)
- Week B: 01:00 UTC (APAC-friendly)
- Week C: 16:00 UTC (PST-friendly)
- First Tuesday of month stays as "canary + blockers" permanent exception
Thoughts?
maya: Works for me. Can we publish the rotation as a single calendar entry with exceptions/rules so people don't get 10 invites?
samir: You can actually attach multiple RRULEs in an .ics but GCal UI is annoying. Quick hack: create three separate recurring events but same title + add a label like "(A)", "(B)", "(C)" and only keep the one that applies visible via calendar subscriptions.
jen: Would prefer a single entry in our team calendar. Users keep seeing duplicates if we add 3 separate entries.
alex: Open to either. If GCal won't do it, maybe we use a single event and update its recurrence programmatically each week via script. Example script using gcal CLI:
```
# pseudo
gcalcli event --title "RFC Sync (rotating)" --when "next Tue 08:00" --repeat "weekly" --until "2026-12-31"
# then update to next slot the night before
```
Not ideal but doable.
maya: Could we instead use a Slack thread + short weekly poll (buttons) that posts the correct Zoom link and updates a single calendar event via calendar-bot? Less heavy-handed.
alex: I like that. calendar-bot — can you do a weekly post + update calendar event when someone clicks? @calendar-bot
calendar-bot: I can. Set me up with the rotate pattern and list of UTC times, and I'll post the weekly slot on Monday with a confirm button. If 3+ folks confirm, I'll update the team calendar event and overwrite the Zoom link. (Requires the team calendar to allow event edits by bot account.)
samir: Also: FYI, the current recurring Zoom invite uses a personal meeting ID that expired. A few folks got 'meeting not found' yesterday. Whoever created the original may need to migrate to the team Zoom account or a new recurring meeting.
jen: I can create the team Zoom recurring meeting and share creds with calendar-bot. Which settings? Waiting room off, record by default OFF, co-hosts allowed.
maya: Also please enable "Use waiting room for guests" off for quicker start for cross-org folks.
jen: Will do. Creating now.
calendar-bot: New event created: "RFC Sync (rotating)". Current week slot: 2026-01-20 08:00 UTC. Zoom link updated: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210 (team meeting). I'll post the Monday poll at 10:00 PT and update the event 18 hours before the meeting.
alex: Awesome, thank you. Can we add a short agenda template to the event description? e.g.,
```
- 5m quick updates
- 20m RFC review (link: https://docs.internal/rfcs/123)
- 10m action items + owners
```
samir: Add the RFC link and a reminder to paste a minimal repro or design snippet in thread if you want in-depth review.
maya: One last ask — please add timezone hints in the calendar description like "08:00 UTC (01:00 PST / 09:00 CET)" so folks don't have to convert.
alex: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll try this rotation next week and iterate.
jen: Event and Zoom set. I'll DM calendar-bot its API token.
calendar-bot: Acknowledged. Poll scheduled for Monday 2026-01-19 10:00 PT. I'll ping this thread with results. :thumbsup:
